# requireTextOutput

<link-summary>Returns the value as a TextOutput, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireTextOutput() — Returns the value as a TextOutput, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/ui</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireTextOutput(
  value: unknown,
  message: string = "Expected a TextOutput object."
): TextOutput;
```

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard looks for the methods that define the type — `getMimeType`, `getContent`. A stub that implements them passes, which is what makes code using this guard testable outside the runtime.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                  | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :--------------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                    | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a TextOutput object."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`TextOutput` — the same value, typed as a TextOutput.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                      |
| :------------------------- | :----------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a TextOutput. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
const output = ContentService.createTextOutput("hi");

requireTextOutput(output); // => output
requireTextOutput({}); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireTextOutput(null); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
